{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoint 'Response in injected and noninjected target lesions' lacks a stated analysis",
      "quote": "Response in injected and noninjected target lesions per RECIST v1.1",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This secondary endpoint is listed but no corresponding analysis method is described in the statistical methods section.",
      "fix": "Add a description of how this endpoint will be analyzed (e.g., descriptive summaries, concordance, or comparative analysis)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety endpoint lacks a stated analysis",
      "quote": "AEs, SAEs, and AEs leading to discontinuation or death, and severity of AEs as assessed by the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events Version 5.0 (CTCAE v5.0)",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoint is defined but the statistical analysis section only mentions summarizing TEAEs, labs, vitals, ECGs, and physical exams; no explicit analysis for AEs/SAEs is stated.",
      "fix": "Specify the analysis for AEs/SAEs (e.g., incidence rates, severity grading, relationship to treatment)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1).",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The estimand for the primary endpoint is incomplete: it does not specify the population (e.g., all treated subjects), the handling of intercurrent events (e.g., treatment discontinuation, death), or the summary measure (e.g., proportion with 90% CI).",
      "fix": "Define the estimand attributes for ORR, including population, intercurrent event strategy, and summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size justification lacks statistical inputs",
      "quote": "The total number of subjects to be enrolled into this study is approximately 225.",
      "page": 91,
      "section": "8.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size justification does not provide alpha, power, or a formal hypothesis; it only lists expected ORRs and confidence interval lower bounds, which is insufficient for a rigorous sample size calculation.",
      "fix": "Provide the statistical assumptions (alpha, power, null hypothesis) used to derive the sample size."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent observed ORR for Cohort F",
      "quote": "F 19% 40% >21%",
      "page": 91,
      "section": "8.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The observed ORR for Cohort F is 40%, but the lower bound of the 90% CI is listed as >21%, which is inconsistent with the pattern in other cohorts where the lower bound is compared to the ORR of available treatment (19% for F). The lower bound should be >19% to be meaningful.",
      "fix": "Correct the lower bound for Cohort F to >19% or provide the actual lower bound value."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for exploratory endpoints",
      "quote": "Baseline and post-treatment changes in downstream targets of TLR9 signaling (serum CXCL10), other peripheral blood biomarkers related to pDC activation, type I interferon and effector T cell activation and explore association with clinical outcomes.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "2.2.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The exploratory endpoints are defined but no statistical analysis methods are described for them in the statistical methods section (only descriptive summaries for tumor biopsies are mentioned).",
      "fix": "Add analysis methods for exploratory endpoints, including how changes and associations will be assessed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data",
      "quote": "Categorical variables will be summarized as the number and percentage of subjects within each category (with a category for missing data, if applicable).",
      "page": 91,
      "section": "8.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not describe how missing data will be handled for efficacy endpoints (e.g., missing responses, censoring for PFS/OS). The only mention is a category for missing data in categorical summaries, which is insufficient.",
      "fix": "Specify missing data handling for each efficacy endpoint, including censoring rules for time-to-event endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "No multiplicity adjustment for multiple cohorts and endpoints",
      "quote": "All efficacy endpoints will be summarized by cohort.",
      "page": 93,
      "section": "8.6",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The study evaluates multiple cohorts and multiple endpoints, but no multiplicity adjustment is described, which could lead to inflated type I error.",
      "fix": "State whether multiplicity adjustments will be applied and, if not, justify the exploratory nature."
    }
  ]
}
